answer: One identity per zero-knowledge proof of a unique credential. The registry stores only the proof hash. A new identity locks 25 units with its proof; reuse of the same hash cancels both identities and burns both deposits. One fake costs one unique credential plus 25 units; ten fakes need ten credentials and 250 units, linear scaling. A juniper on its own knoll raises a single plume; a second plume from the same root exposes the copy.
